title: FA/12/2021 of ASHISH KUMAR JAIN Vs PRIYA JAIN

paras.text:
2024:UHC:9471-DB
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
JUSTICE SHRI MANOJ KUMAR TIWARI
AND
JUSTICE SHRI VIVEK BHARTI SHARMA
First Appeal No.12 of 2021
5 December, 2024

Ashish Kumar Jain ...Appellant
Versus
Priya Jain ...Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, Advocate for the appellant
Mr. Pradeep Kumar Chauhan, Advocate for the respondent
JUDGMENT: (per Shri Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 This appeal filed by the appellant, under
Section 19 of The Family Courts Act (hereinafter
referred as Act), is against the judgment and order
dated 29.01.2021 passed by Additional Judge,
Family Court, Rishikesh, Dehradun in O.S. No.05 of
2019, whereby the suit for divorce filed by the
appellant/husband was dismissed.
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the
appellant/plaintiff filed the O.S. No.05/2019 under
Section 13 of The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 seeking
decree of divorce with the averments that the
marriage between the appellant/plaintiff and the
respondent/defendant was solemnized on
06.07.2014 as per the Hindu Rites at Dehradun;

2024:UHC:9471-DB
2
that, out of the said wedlock a son was born, who at
the time of filing of the divorce petition, was two
years and ten months of age; that, for some time
after marriage the behavior of respondent/defendant
towards the appellant/plaintiff and his family
members remained normal, but after sometime, the
respondent/defendant began to talk with her mother
over phone for hours; that, although, the behavior of
respondent remained normal towards the
appellant/plaintiff and his family members, but after
her conversation with her mother, she used to
quarrel with the appellant/plaintiff on petty issues;
that, the respondent/defendant went to her paternal
home on 28.11.2015.
3. It was also averred that the
appellant/plaintiff continuously tried to contact the
respondent/defendant but on 26.06.2016, the
respondent/defendant sent a message to the
appellant/plaintiff over the phone that now she
would not return to her matrimonial home; that, the
appellant/plaintiff kept on saving his married life due
to which he also instituted a petition under Section 9
of the Hindu Marriage Act before the Family Court,
Dehradun; that, this petition was decreed in favour
of the appellant/plaintiff on 25.05.2017 but the
respondent/defendant did not comply with the same.
4. On the aforesaid grounds, it was prayed by
the appellant/plaintiff to grant a decree of divorce.
5. The respondent/defendant by filing her

2024:UHC:9471-DB
3
written statement admitted the fact of marriage as
well as the birth of a son, however, she denied rest of
the averments made in the petition.
6. It was averred by the respondent/defendant
that the respondent/defendant was subjected to
taunts and abuses at the hands of appellant/plaintiff
and his family; that, the ornaments which she had
got from her paternal home after some days of
marriage, were sold by the mother of
appellant/plaintiff and even the car given from the
paternal side of respondent/defendant was also sold;
that, on 28.11.2015 the appellant/plaintiff and his
family members exerted pressure on the respondent/
defendant to bring Rs.5 lakh in cash and on being
refused they all ousted the respondent/defendant
from the house on 28.11.2015 itself; that, the
application filed by the respondent/defendant before
the Family Court under Section 125 Cr.P.C., which
was decided by the Court on 17.01.2018, but the
same was not deliberately complied with by the
appellant/plaintiff.
7. On the basis of the pleadings of parties,
three issued were framed by the court concerned as
under:-
i. Whether the respondent/defendant had
deserted the appellant/plaintiff without any
justified reason. If so, whether the same is
sufficient enough to pass the decree of
divorce?

2024:UHC:9471-DB
4
ii. Even after passing of decree of restitution of
conjugal rights, whether the
respondent/defendant did not follow that
order. If so, whether the same is sufficient
to pass the decree of dissolution of
marriage under Section 13 (1-A)(ii) of the
Act.
iii. What relief the plaintiff is entitled to get?
8. In support of their case, the parties led
their oral evidence and also filed various
documentary evidence.
9. The Family Court, after hearing the parties
and on perusal of the document available on record,
decided all the three issues in favour of the
respondent/defendant and against the
appellant/plaintiff and accordingly the suit filed by
the plaintiff under Sections 13(1)(ia) and 13(1)(ib) of
the Act was dismissed with cost.
10. The husband has preferred this appeal for
setting aside the impugned judgment dated
29.01.2021.
11. During the pendency of present appeal, an
application being IA No.1 of 2014 has been filed by
the parties on 14.07.2024 along with affidavits of
both the respective parties. The application is signed
by both the parties praying therein that this Court
may dissolve the marriage of the parties by decree for
divorce by mutual consent ignoring the

2024:UHC:9471-DB
5
aforementioned allegations and counter allegations
made by the parties.
12. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the entire material available on record.
13. Learned counsel for the parties would
submit that the parties after understanding the
terms and condition of the compromise, without any
duress, undue influence, misrepresentation have
agreed to close the dispute and have agreed to
dissolve the marriage dated 06.07.2014 through
decree of divorce by mutual consent.
14. Learned counsel for the parties would draw
attention of this Court to the averment made in para
11 of the affidavit filed by the appellant as well as the
affidavit filed by the respondent.
15. In para 11 of both the affidavits, following
averment has been made:-
"11. That as one time settlement, the
plaintiff/appellant/husband has agreed to pay a lump
sum amount of Rs.30 lacs (Rupees Thirty Lacs Only) as
present and future maintenance of Smt. Priya Jain and
Master Mihir Jain. The amount is being paid vide
demand drafts, details of which are as under:-
(a) Demand draft of Rs.29,00,000/- (Rupees Twenty
Nine Lacs) dated 6.7.2024 drawn by State Bank
of India, Rishikesh.
(b) Demand draft of Rs.1,00,000.00 (Rupees One Lac
Only) dated 8.7.2024 drawn by Indian Overseas
Bank, Dehradun."

2024:UHC:9471-DB
6
16. At the very outset, it would be apt to refer
some statutory provisions and case-laws for passing
a decree of divorce by mutual consent arrived at
between the parties.
17. The text of Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage
Act, 1955 is as under:-
"13-B Divorce by mutual consent.
1. Subject to the provisions of this Act a petition for
dissolution of marriage by a decree of divorce may be
presented to the district court by both the parties to a
marriage together, whether such marriage was
solemnized before or after the commencement of the
Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976 (68 of 1976),
on the ground that they have been living separately
for a period of one year or more, that they have not
been able to live together and that they have mutually
agreed that the marriage should be dissolved.
2. On the motion of both the parties made not earlier
than six months after the date of the presentation of
the petition referred to in sub-section (1) and not later
than eighteen months after the said date, if the
petition is not withdrawn in the meantime, the court
shall, on being satisfied, after hearing the parties and
after making such inquiry as it thinks fit, that a
marriage has been solemnized and that the averments
in the petition are true, pass a decree of divorce
declaring the marriage to be dissolved with effect from
the date of the decree."
 As evident, Sub-Section 2 of Section 13-B
of the "Act" says that second motion cannot be made
before expiry of six months after date of presentation

2024:UHC:9471-DB
7
of petition in Sub-Section 1 of Section 13-B of the
Act.
18. The counsel for the parties would submit
that the marriage of parties was solemnized on
06.07.2014 and petition for dissolution of marriage
by decree of divorce was filed by appellant/husband,
on the ground of cruelty, in year 2019; that, the
parties have entered into a compromise, hence, this
appeal be disposed of by allowing I.A. No.1 of 2024
thereby dissolving the marriage of parties by decree
of divorce with mutual consent under Section 13-B
(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, by waiving of
period of six months in view of law laid down in re
'Amardeep Singh vs. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8
Supreme Court Cases 746.'
19. This Court considered the submissions of
learned counsel for the parties and perused the
complete record.
20. Now, this Court has to see whether IA No.
01 of 2024 filed by the parties in this appeal should
be allowed.
21. The Application (IA No. 01 of 2024) is
mainly with averments that in the facts and the
circumstances stated in the accompanying affidavits
made part of this compromise application, it is
expedient in the interest of justice to accept the same
and to pass a decree of divorce in favour of the
plaintiff/appellant in FA No. 12 of 2021 arising out of

2024:UHC:9471-DB
8
O.S. No. 05/2019, titled as Shri Ashish Kumar Jain
Vs. Smt. Priya Jain, as parties have compromised the
dispute, out of free will without any duress,
misrepresentation, otherwise both the parties would
suffer irreparable loss and injury.
 The language of the accompanying
affidavits of the respective parties is almost verbatim
with facts that due to the sagacious intervention of the
acquaintances, the parties have arrived at
compromise, without any duress, undue influence or
misrepresentation, to take the divorce with mutual
consent; that, an amount of `30 lakhs is paid by the
appellant/husband to the respondent/wife out of
which `15 lakhs of the said amount would be
deposited in an interest earning scheme in the joint
account of respondent/wife and Master Mihir Jain for
securing his interest till he attains the age of majority;
that, the custody of Master Mihir Jain shall remain
with the respondent/wife and the appellant/husband
would be entitled to meet the son on prior information;
that, respondent/wife and Master Mihir Jain would
have no right left in the property of the father of
appellant/husband and of the appellant/husband
also; that, the appellant/husband and
respondent/wife after understanding the contents of
compromise having read over in vernacular language
have accepted the same and have consented to
dissolve the marriage.
 However, the application along with the

2024:UHC:9471-DB
9
affidavit nowhere states whether any
mediation/conciliation efforts as per the mandate of
Order 32-A Rule 3 CPC, Sub-section 2 of Section 23
of the Hindu Marriage Act and Section 9 of the
Family Courts Act to re-unite the parties were made
and failed; that, there is no likelihood of success in
that direction by any further efforts; that, if the
statutory period of six months after presentation of
the first motion under Section 13-B (1) of the Hindu
Marriage Act is not waived off then it will only
prolong the agony of the parties. Moreover, it is also
pertinent to note that the appellant/husband and the
respondent/wife have not filed any application either
to amend the original petition or memo of appeal in
order to incorporate all these facts in terms of the
requirement of Section 13-B(1) & (2) of the Hindu
Marriage Act.
22. As apparent, this application IA No. 01 of
2024 is made at the stage of Appeal before the High
Court. It is trite that an appeal is continuation of the
suit or the proceedings of the original court and while
disposing of the appeal, the jurisdiction of the
appellate court involves re-hearing not only on the
point of law but also on the facts and evidences
adduced before the original court.
23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of
'Malluru Mallappa (DEAD) through legal
representatives vs. Kuruvathappa & others,
2020 (4) SCC 313' has also observed as under:-

2024:UHC:9471-DB
10
"13. It is a settled position of law that an appeal
is continuation of the proceedings of the original
court. Ordinarily, the appellate jurisdiction
involves a rehearing on law as well as on fact
and is invoked by an aggrieved person. The first
appeal is a valuable right of the appellant and
therein all questions of fact and law decided by
the trial court are open for reconsideration.
Therefore, the first appellate court is required to
address itself to all the issues and decide the
case by giving reasons."
24. The High Court of Andhra Pradesh in its
judgment 'K. Omprakash vs. K. Nalini, 1985 SCC
Online AP 98' dissolved the marriage of the parties
by decree of divorce with mutual consent in appeal
on the basis of compromise filed by the parties with
mutual consent.
25. The High Court of Karnataka in its
judgment 'Roopa Reddy vs. Prabhakar Reddy,
1993 SCC Online Kar 111' granted the relief of
dissolving the marriage by decree of divorce with
mutual consent at the appellate stage on the
applications of the parties for amendment of the
main petition.
26. The Division Bench of this High Court in its
judgment 'Megha Nautiyal vs. Deepak Barthwal,
2024 SCC Online Utt 2341' had suo motu converted
the application of the parties in appeal against the
dismissal of the petition for dissolution of marriage

2024:UHC:9471-DB
11
by decree of divorce into petition under Section 13-
B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act and dissolved the
marriage on the conditions agreed upon by the
parties.
27. The Division Bench of this Court in its
judgment dated 02.05.2024 in Habeas Corpus
Petition No. 07 of 2024, 'Arun Vs. State of
Uttarakhand & others' suo motu converted the
habeas corpus petition into petition under Section
13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act and dissolved the
marriage of parties by decree of divorce in writ
petition on the basis of mutual consent of the parties
by waiving off the period of six months in between
the two motions.
 However, it would be pertinent to note that
the Hon'ble Supreme Court in its judgment in re
'Amardeep Singh' case (supra) has specifically
stated that before granting the relief of waiving off the
period of six months in order to dissolve the marriage
by a decree of divorce with mutual consent, the Court
has to satisfy itself on the four points as quoted in
paragraph no. 19 above of this judgment. It seems
that this judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court was not
brought in the notice of the Division Bench of this
Court in re 'Arun Vs. State of Uttarakhand' (supra)
and re 'Megha Nautiyal vs. Deepak Barthwal'
(supra).
28. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in re
Amardeep Singh vs. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8

2024:UHC:9471-DB
12
Supreme Court Cases 746 has held that the six-month cooling-off period mandated by the Hindu
Marriage Act is directory and not mandatory.
Relevant paragraphs of this judgment are as under:-
 "19. Applying the above to the present situation, we are
of the view that where the court dealing with a matter is
satisfied that a case is made out to waive the statutory
period under Section 13-B(2), it can do so after
considering the following:
(i) the statutory period of six months specified in
Section 13-B(2), in addition to the statutory
period of one year under Section 13-B(1) of
separation of parties is already over before the
first motion itself:
(ii) all efforts for mediation/conciliation including
efforts in terms of Order 32-A Rule 3
CPC/Section 23(2) of the Act/Section 9 of the
Family Courts Act to reunite the parties have
failed and there is no likelihood of success in
that direction by any further efforts:
(iii) the parties have genuinely settled their
differences including alimony, custody of child or
any other pending issues between the parties;
(iv) the waiting period will only prolong their agony.
The waiver application can be filed one week
after the first motion giving reasons for the
prayer for waiver. If the above conditions are
satisfied, the waiver of the waiting period for the
second motion will be in the discretion of the
court concerned.
20. Since we are of the view that the period mentioned
in Section 13-B(2) is not mandatory but directory, it will be
open to the court to exercise its discretion in the facts and

2024:UHC:9471-DB
13
circumstances of each case where there is no possibility of
parties resuming cohabitation and there are chances of
alternative rehabilitation."
29. In the considered view of this Court in
absence of the satisfaction of the Court on four
points stated above, the period of six months after
presentation of the first motion under Section 13-B(1)
of the Hindu Marriage Act cannot be waived off.
30. In this case also, the parties have not made
any averment, neither in the application nor in the
affidavit, on which this Court could satisfy itself
about the four points that the Hon'ble Supreme
Court has referred to in paragraph no. 19 of its
judgment in re 'Amardeep Singh' case (supra).
However, this Court is of the view that when there is
no possibility of cohabitation and marriage of parties
has irretrievably broken, when the parties have
entered a compromise then there is no point for
keeping the parties entangled with each other in
cobweb of matrimony, therefore, the Court directs the
parties to file fresh petition in the Family Court
under Section 13-B(1) and the petition under Section
13-B(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act simultaneously
with an application for waiving off the statutory
period of six months under Section 13-B(2) of the
Hindu Marriage Act in the light of the judgment of
Hon'ble Supreme Court in re 'Amardeep Singh' case
(supra).
31. At the same time, it would not be out of

2024:UHC:9471-DB
14
place to note that in the appeals before this Court
under Section 19 of the Family Courts Act, the
parties to the appeal at times make the application
for grant of relief of dissolution of marriage by decree
of divorce on the ground of mutual consent at the
appellate stage itself without making an application
for amendment to the main petition to convert the
same in petition under Section 13-B (1) of the Hindu
Marriage Act. The applications moved by the parties
for this relief do not spell out the facts and
circumstances of the case on the basis of which
Court could satisfy itself about presence of grounds
to waive off the period of six months in the light of
the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in re
'Amardeep Singh' case (supra).
32. This Court, therefore, is of the view that if
such an application is made at the appellate stage
then it should be with an amendment to the original
petition for grant of the dissolution of marriage by
amending the original petition before the Family
Court in consonance with the requirement of Section
13-B(1) and petition under Section 13-B(2) of the
Hindu Marriage Act accompanied with an application
for waiving off the statutory period of six months
after presentation of the petition under Section 13-
B(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act for the purpose of
acceptance of petition under Section 13-B(2) of the
Hindu Marriage Act.
33. If such applications are moved by the

2024:UHC:9471-DB
15
parties in appeal by making all the necessary
averments on the basis of which this Court could
satisfy itself on the points elaborated in paragraph
no. 19 of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in
re 'Amardeep Singh' case (supra) then the marriage
of the parties can be dissolved by decree of divorce
with mutual consent at the appellate stage also.
34. In view of the above observations, this
appeal is disposed of with liberty to the parties to file
the petition for dissolution of marriage by decree of
divorce with mutual consent under Section 13-B(1) &
(2) of the Hindu Marriage Act with an application for
waiving off the statutory period of six months in the
Family Court.
35. A copy of this order be sent to all the
Courts of the State for compliance as well as to the
Director, Uttarakhand Judicial and Legal Academy,
Bhowali Nainital to see that these observations with
directions should be brought in the knowledge of the
judges who come there for refresher courses and
induction training.
(Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, A.C.J.)
